title: 2024 HMMT February Guts Problem 25
statement: Point \(P\) is inside a square \(A B C D\) such that \(\angle A P B=135^{\circ}, P C=12\), and \(P D=15\). Compute the area of this square.

solutions.text:
Let \(x=A P\) and \(y=B P\). Rotate \(\triangle B A P\) by \(90^{\circ}\) around \(B\) to get \(\triangle B C Q\). Then, \(\triangle B P Q\) is rightisosceles, and from \(\angle B Q C=135^{\circ}\), we get \(\angle P Q C=90^{\circ}\). Therefore, by Pythagorean's theorem, \(P C^{2}=x^{2}+2 y^{2}\). Similarly, \(P D^{2}=y^{2}+2 x^{2}\).
Thus, \(y^{2}=\frac{2 P C^{2}-P D^{2}}{3}=21\), and similarly \(x^{2}=102 \Longrightarrow x y=3 \sqrt{238}\).
Thus, by the Law of Cosines, the area of the square is

\[\begin{aligned}
A B^{2} & =A P^{2}+B P^{2}-2 \cos \left(135^{\circ}\right)(A P)(B P) \\
& =x^{2}+y^{2}+\sqrt{2} x y \\
& =123+6 \sqrt{119}
\end{aligned}\]
